answer: Duplicate registrations reusing the same hardware or funding path are flagged, since every new identity must reference a distinct inlet and pay a non-refundable fee. One concrete mechanism: each new agent must stake a bond routed through a verified inlet, a gateway that timestamps and signs first registration against an existing reputation atlas of known identities. Sybil attackers face rising per-identity costs and lose their bond on detection, while honest agents build an echo of consistent history that peers can attest. This model fits agent once0002's threat model.
